s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bony mass of the forehead
salient_findings: Painless, slowly progressive mass on the left forehead
Diffuse sclerosis and intra-trabecular fibrosis on core biopsy
key_facts: 45-year-old man
History of systemic lupus erythematosus, well controlled
No immunomodulatory therapy
30 × 20 mm mass on the left forehead
Mass progressed over 1 year
Previous excision of a similar frontal bone lesion
Previous lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia
No headaches or neurologic symptoms
CT scan showed homogenous matrix expansion of the frontal bone
Fine-needle aspiration cytology excluded multiple myeloma
Core biopsy demonstrated diffuse sclerosis and intra-trabecular fibrosis
Preoperative laboratory tests were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Previous diagnosis of fibrous dysplasia and current biopsy findings suggestive of fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Monostotic fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of a similar frontal bone lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive bony mass of the forehead, although less likely given the patient's age and lack of familial history

shortlist.label: Osteofibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical and radiological features to fibrous dysplasia, but less common

shortlist.label: Paget's disease of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, Paget's disease can present with a bony mass and bone resorption, but typically occurs in older adults

raw.rationale: The patient's history of a similar lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia, the current lesion's appearance on CT scan with a ground-glass appearance and homogenous matrix expansion, and the core biopsy demonstrating diffuse sclerosis and intra-trabecular fibrosis are all consistent with fibrous dysplasia. The term 'monostotic' specifically refers to fibrous dysplasia affecting a single bone, which aligns with the patient's presentation of a lesion confined to the frontal bone.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: While the diagnosis is correct, 'monostotic fibrous dysplasia' is more specific as it indicates the condition is limited to one bone.

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: Cherubism typically presents in childhood with bilateral involvement of the jawbones, which does not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Osteofibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Osteofibrous dysplasia is more commonly associated with the tibia and fibula, and its histological features can be distinguished from fibrous dysplasia.

rejected.label: Paget's disease of bone
rejected.why: Paget's disease typically affects older adults and involves an initial osteolytic phase followed by a mixed phase and finally a sclerotic phase, with elevated alkaline phosphatase levels, which is not described in the patient's case.
